claim: The PubMed abstract for a multi-setting observational study reports 1,002.3 hours of observations derived from three earlier studies at a teaching hospital in Sydney, Australia: emergency department doctors (n=40), ward doctors (n=57), and ward nurses (n=104). The study compared task-switching with multitasking and used random-intercepts logistic regression to examine associated factors and variation between clinicians. Strategy use was associated with the nature and complexity of work and the person the clinician was working with; in some settings, time of day, day of week, or the previously chosen strategy also mattered. After the included factors, the abstract reports significant between-clinician variation for ED doctors (p=0.04) and ward staff (p=0.03). These findings are bounded to the reported groups and settings. The abstract does not establish transferable covariates, demographic effects, a variation distribution, effect sizes, or numeric calibration parameters.
